Scheme Structure

Understanding the Combined Central & Uttar Pradesh Solar Subsidy

The Government of India launched the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana to provide direct financial assistance to Indian households installing grid-connected rooftop solar power plants. In Uttar Pradesh, the state government provides an additional supplementary subsidy administered through UPNEDA (Uttar Pradesh New and Renewable Energy Development Agency).

Eligible residential consumers may receive up to ₹1.08 lakh in combined central and Uttar Pradesh support, subject to current scheme rules, eligibility, approved vendor requirements and successful installation/verification.

Because Ayodhya has been chosen by the Uttar Pradesh administration as a showcase Model Solar City, administrative coordination between local DISCOM divisions (Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd / Purvanchal) and solar vendors is closely monitored to streamline consumer approvals.

Please note: Government subsidy rules, eligibility, procedures and amounts can change. Customers should verify current details on official government portals before making a purchase decision.

To verify the latest central guidelines directly, visit the official national portal at pmsuryaghar.gov.in.

Subsidy Summary at a Glance

  • 1 kW System: ₹30,000 Central + ₹15,000 UP = ₹45,000 Total
  • 2 kW System: ₹60,000 Central + ₹30,000 UP = ₹90,000 Total
  • 3 kW System: ₹78,000 Central + ₹30,000 UP = ₹1,08,000 Total
  • Above 3 kW: Capped at ₹78,000 Central + ₹30,000 UP = ₹1,08,000 Total

Who Qualifies

Eligibility Requirements for Ayodhya Consumers

To successfully receive the combined subsidy, your installation must satisfy the following fundamental requirements:

1. Domestic Electricity Consumer Category

The connection tariff code must be domestic residential (LMV-1). Commercial meters (LMV-2), industrial connections, or agricultural pump connections do not qualify for residential CFA.

2. Grid-Connected System Only

The system must be a grid-tied installation connected via an approved bi-directional net meter. Off-grid systems with independent batteries are not covered by the PM Surya Ghar subsidy.

3. Clear Roof Rights

The applicant must own the house or possess valid legal rights to utilize the rooftop space without encumbrance. In multi-family dwellings, a no-objection certificate (NOC) from co-owners is required.

4. DCR-Compliant Solar Modules

Only modules utilizing domestically manufactured solar cells (Domestic Content Requirement) and listed under the MNRE Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) can be installed.

5. Single Subsidy Per Connection

Central financial assistance can only be claimed once against a unique electricity consumer number.

Application Walkthrough

The 5-Step Official Subsidy Application Procedure

How an application moves from online registration to net metering and direct bank transfer (DBT).

  1. 1

    Check Eligibility

    Residential connection in your name, a suitable roof, and no previous solar subsidy on the same connection.

  2. 2

    Apply Through the Official Portal

    Register on pmsuryaghar.gov.in with your state, DISCOM and electricity consumer number, then submit the rooftop solar application.

  3. 3

    Feasibility / Approval

    Your DISCOM reviews the application and issues technical feasibility before installation begins.

  4. 4

    Install Rooftop Solar

    The system is installed by a vendor registered for the scheme. Plant details are then submitted on the portal along with the net meter request.

  5. 5

    Inspection / Commissioning / Subsidy Process

    After net metering and DISCOM inspection, the commissioning report is generated and the subsidy is processed to your bank account as per scheme rules.

We can guide you through the installation and documentation process. Approval and subsidy release are decided by the government and your DISCOM, so no installer can guarantee them.

Checklist

Documents Required for PM Surya Ghar Application

Keep digital scans or clear photos of these four essential records ready before commencing your registration.

  • Recent Electricity Bill

    Must be in the name of the applicant with consumer number clearly visible (MVVNL / Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam). Bill must have no outstanding arrears.

  • Aadhaar Card of Consumer

    The name and mobile number on the Aadhaar card must align with the national PM Surya Ghar registration and bank account records.

  • Cancelled Bank Cheque / Bank Passbook

    Photocopy or scanned image of a cancelled cheque clearly showing the applicant’s name, bank account number, and IFSC code for direct DBT credit.

  • Terrace Rights Proof / Electricity Meter Photo

    Clear photograph of the electricity meter showing current reading and serial number, alongside proof of roof access or no-objection certificate (NOC) if shared roof.

Caution & Warnings

5 Common Mistakes That Delay or Disqualify Subsidies

Avoid these frequent pitfalls reported by consumers across Uttar Pradesh.

  • Mismatched Bank Account Names: The bank account submitted for subsidy disbursement must match the electricity consumer name. Subsidies cannot be credited into third-party or business accounts for domestic connections.
  • Installing Non-DCR / Non-Approved Panels: Under PM Surya Ghar regulations, all solar modules must use Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) compliant solar cells manufactured in India. Installing uncertified or non-DCR modules completely disqualifies the plant from central subsidies.
  • Starting Work Before DISCOM Feasibility Approval: Physical installation must not precede technical feasibility approval issued by your local electricity distribution division on the national portal.
  • Expecting PM Surya Ghar Subsidy for Commercial Meters: The central financial assistance of up to ₹78,000 is strictly reserved for residential consumer connections. Applying under commercial or industrial tariff categories results in immediate portal rejection.
  • Incorrect Mobile Number Linked to Bank / Portal: All OTP authentications, milestone tracking SMS, and bank DBT validations depend on the active mobile number registered during step 1.

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions on Solar Subsidies

Have a question that isn’t answered here?

Ask on WhatsApp

How does PM Surya Ghar subsidy work?

PM Surya Ghar is a central government scheme that gives financial assistance to eligible residential consumers for grid-connected rooftop solar. You register on the official portal (pmsuryaghar.gov.in) with your electricity consumer details, receive feasibility approval from your electricity distribution company (DISCOM), get the system installed by a vendor registered for the scheme, and complete net metering and inspection. After commissioning, the subsidy is released to your bank account as per scheme rules. Read our Ayodhya solar subsidy guide for each step.

How much subsidy can I receive in Uttar Pradesh?

Central assistance under PM Surya Ghar is currently ₹30,000 for 1 kW, ₹60,000 for 2 kW and ₹78,000 for 3 kW, with ₹78,000 as the cap for larger residential systems. Uttar Pradesh adds a state subsidy of ₹15,000 per kW up to ₹30,000. Eligible residential consumers may therefore receive up to ₹1.08 lakh in combined support, subject to current scheme rules, eligibility, vendor requirements and successful installation and verification.

Is solar subsidy available for commercial properties?

The PM Surya Ghar central financial assistance is meant for residential households, so shops, offices and other commercial connections should not expect that subsidy. Businesses can still benefit from lower electricity bills, and tax-paying businesses may have tax considerations worth discussing with their accountant. See commercial solar.

What is net metering?

Net metering uses a bi-directional meter that records both the electricity your solar system sends to the grid and the electricity you take from it. You are billed for the difference. It is arranged through your DISCOM under the rules of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission. Our net metering guide explains it with examples.

How does a grid-connected solar system work?

Solar panels produce DC electricity, which the inverter converts to AC for your home. Your appliances use solar power first; extra power flows to the grid through the net meter, and at night you draw from the grid as usual. For safety, a standard on-grid system switches off during a power cut. If you need backup, a hybrid system with batteries is the option to discuss.

How much does solar panel installation cost in Ayodhya?

The cost depends mainly on system size (kW), the type of solar panels, the inverter, the height and design of the mounting structure, wiring distance and any net-metering related work. A battery adds significantly to the price. Because these vary from roof to roof, we give an itemised quotation after a site assessment rather than a one-size price. Eligible residential consumers may reduce their net cost through PM Surya Ghar central support and the additional Uttar Pradesh subsidy. See our solar price guide for the full list of cost factors.

Can I contact a solar installer in Ayodhya through WhatsApp?

Yes. Message us on WhatsApp at +91 9580659559. Sending a photo of a recent electricity bill and a few photos of your roof helps us give you a quicker preliminary idea before a site visit.
